TC-06/S10.title: Midnight edges: status set at 23:59, set at 00:01, a future-stamped day, lists open across midnight, a second device
TC-06/S10.detail: Our own boundary case (2026-10-15 review: record-only). PW, local stack. Device A's clock started at Oct 14 23:57 JST (behind the real clock); at 23:59 P1 (Hospital) and R1 (Nursing Home) were set to New Admission on their charts (stored new@2026-10-14); the Hospital and Nursing Home lists stayed open in two tabs while the clock ran past midnight; at 00:01 P2 / R2 were set to Consult (stored consult@2026-10-15); P3 / R3 carried a future-stamped day 2026-10-16 (what a device a day ahead stores on main). Seen: at 00:00:38, no reload, the open lists already read Follow-up for P1 / R1 (client-side render; the server still had new@2026-10-14), and by the 10-minute lifecycle repeat the roll was stored (follow-up@2026-10-15); P2 / R2 stayed Consult that day; device B on the real clock showed the same badges as A. 'Next midnight' emulated by moving every stored day back one day: P2 / R2 rolled to Follow-up, but P3 / R3 still read New Admission and rolled only a day later - the device-clock day stored by a fast device (known B18, TFA-92584 AC 8). Q1 (recorded): the roll follows the physician's local midnight (00:00 JST), not server UTC midnight (09:00 JST).
